component: Intel safestringlib (vendored subset) evaluated as candidate component, not an automatic dependency

upstream.license: MIT (LICENSE: Copyright (c) 2014-2018 Intel Corporation; plus Cisco Systems 2012-2013 MIT notice)
upstream.archived_detail: Upstream README states THIS PROJECT IS ARCHIVED; Intel will not provide or guarantee development, maintenance, bug fixes, new releases or updates. GitHub reports archived by owner on 2026-07-20 and read-only (discontinuation notice commit 68c2e2e, 2026-06-23).

build_integration.evidence: scripts/build_safecrt.sh line 116: '# Intel safestringlib retained in third_party for provenance/reference only; not compiled/linked.' The compile loop (lines 92-114) lists only third_party/safeclib/src/** sources plus stdlib/safe/src/*.c and exceptions4c.c; the ar command (line 125) archives only sc_*.o, w_*.o, e4c_*.o. No intel-safestringlib object is produced.
build_integration.standalone_cmake_target: third_party/intel-safestringlib/CMakeLists.txt defines a standalone STATIC library cplus_safestringlib compiling 16 vendored .c files with -include rename_symbols.h (cplus_upstream_* symbol prefix) and __STDC_WANT_LIB_EXT1__=0.
build_integration.cmake_reference_evidence: grep for cplus_safestringlib|intel-safestringlib in all CMakeLists.txt matches only the Intel directory's own CMakeLists.txt; no parent project CMakeLists adds this subdirectory.
build_integration.snprintf_support_evidence: safeclib/snprintf_support.c is vendored but appears neither in scripts/build_safecrt.sh compile loop nor in the Intel CMakeLists.txt source list.
build_integration.conclusion: Intel sources are NOT compiled or linked into libcplus_safecrt.a. Only rurban/safeclib is the linked checked backend. The Intel CMakeLists is an unreferenced standalone artifact.

duplicate_vs_unique_analysis.summary: The vendored Intel subset is essentially a strict subset of rurban/safeclib's already-linked API surface. 67 of 73 Intel declarations are either already integrated in C+ (16) or available in the vendored rurban safeclib tree (51). Only 2 declarations (wmemset_s, wcpcpy_s) are absent from rurban safeclib, and both are declaration-only in the Intel subset (no .c vendored). The 4 snprintf_s_* typed wrappers are Intel-specific contracts with no exact safeclib counterpart, but C+ already has a stronger variadic checked snprintf_s; Intel's source for them is not compiled.
notable_findings: Intel headers do NOT declare generic snprintf_s, sprintf_s, or vsnprintf_s; those names exist only in rurban safeclib (include/safe_str_lib.h) and the C+ facade (stdlib/safe/safe_format.h).
Intel's memset_s is 3-arg (dest, dmax, value) whereas Annex K, rurban safeclib and C+ use 4-arg (dest, dmax, value, n); it is therefore not a drop-in.

Intel's strnlen_s loop is bounds-first (`while (dmax && *dest)`) and avoids the one-byte over-read that rurban upstream had; C+ already carries a local patch for rurban, so this Intel detail provides no remaining benefit.

The archived status removes any prospect of upstream fixes or security patches; relying on Intel code would create a maintenance liability with no upside given full duplication by an actively vendored backend.

recommendation.decision: KEEP AS REFERENCE-ONLY; DO NOT INTEGRATE ANY INTEL FILES
rationale: All 15 compiled-capable Intel implementations duplicate rurban/safeclib APIs that C+ already links and tests.
51 additional Intel declarations are available in rurban/safeclib if ever needed, without importing a second backend.
The only 2 unique declarations (wmemset_s, wcpcpy_s) have no Intel implementation in the vendored subset and no demonstrated C+ need.
The 4 Intel typed snprintf wrappers use a weaker partial parser than C+ safe_format.h and are not compiled by any project build.
Upstream is archived and read-only (2026-07-20); Intel provides no maintenance, bug fixes, or security patches.

Integrating Intel would either collide with CRT/safeclib symbols (needs the cplus_upstream_* prefix) or create two competing checked backends with divergent contracts (3-arg memset_s, zero-length policies, *diff vs raw difference).
docs/libc/SAFER_UPSTREAM_INTEGRATION.md and docs/libc/DEPENDENCIES.md already record the reference-only decision; no source changes are warranted.

if_integration_were_ever_required.build_requirement: Must retain -include rename_symbols.h (cplus_upstream_* prefix) or equivalent -D prefixing, and must NOT be added to scripts/build_safecrt.sh's sc_*.o archive.

warnings: third_party/intel-safestringlib/CMakeLists.txt can build a standalone cplus_safestringlib static library from 16 Intel .c files; it is not referenced by any parent CMakeLists and not used by scripts/build_safecrt.sh, but someone invoking it directly would produce a second, differently-prefixed checked backend. Do not add it to the main build.

54 of 73 public declarations are declaration-only in the vendored subset — compiling code that calls them against the Intel headers alone would produce undefined references. This reinforces reference-only status.
snprintf_support.c is vendored but compiled by neither build path; its four `inline` definitions are therefore unbuildable as shipped.

Error-code contracts differ: Intel returns positive constraint codes (RCNEGATE is a no-op outside __KERNEL__), while the generic C+ snprintf_s family returns negative values on error; do not treat the two as interchangeable.
RSIZE_MAX differs: Intel safe_lib.h defines 256MB; C+ RSIZE_MAX_MEM is SIZE_MAX>>1. A future integration would change which sizes are rejected.
Provenance files were copied at commit f4491915 (SAFEC_VERSION_STRING 1.3.0); upstream master was later archived, so this snapshot is frozen and cannot receive fixes.
